stage1.impression: A dark doorway frame that looks into a small slatted room. Two identical red-glowing acrylic speakers stand on either side of a rainbow neon ring sphere on a stone plinth. The top and left third of the frame are an almost empty brown-black mass, the large flat oak panel on the right is brighter than the room it frames, and there are no people, glasses or records, so it reads as a CG showroom vignette or a gallery installation, not a lived-in bar. The speakers' glow is saturated and slightly blown, and the frosted acrylic reads more as lit plastic signage than as thick cast acrylic. As it stands a design magazine would not publish it as a specific, well-made place: the architecture that makes the bar specific (the slotted oak face, the amber band, the bar itself) is lost in black, and what is left is generic.
